questions.label: Water availability
questions.prompt: Is the water available to land and plants changing?

variables.why: Rain is the input of the land water balance.
Root-zone soil moisture represents estimated water stored in the soil available to plants.
The top 10 cm respond fastest to rain and drying.
Evapotranspiration is the water returned to the air; where water is scarce it follows rain.
Vegetation would show the biological response — not processed yet.
River flow would show the hydrological response — not processed yet.

cards.title: Regional trends of Antofagasta and Los Lagos differ in MERRA-2

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27); test on the difference series
analysis.correction: nominal p applies (planned comparison); q across 120 pairs shown

checks.scope: NASA regional mean recomputed on the station's months; the station is one point
checks.dependency: point observation (different spatial support); may be assimilated by the reanalyses

checks.source: ERA5 (ECMWF reanalysis) at 5 grid points, compared with MERRA-2 at the same points
checks.scope: ERA5 and NASA at the same five grid points (not a regional mean)
checks.dependency: partially dependent: a different reanalysis that assimilates many of the same observations as MERRA-2

checks.scope: NASA regional mean recomputed on the station's months; the station is one point
checks.dependency: point observation (different spatial support); may be assimilated by the reanalyses

checks.source: ERA5 (ECMWF reanalysis) at 5 grid points, compared with MERRA-2 at the same points
checks.scope: ERA5 and NASA at the same five grid points (not a regional mean)
checks.dependency: partially dependent: a different reanalysis that assimilates many of the same observations as MERRA-2

cards.can: In MERRA-2 the regional-mean trend of Antofagasta is larger than that of Los Lagos; the difference is statistically significant.
cards.cannot: A significant trend in a regional mean does not show that warming is spatially uniform: within Antofagasta, the coastal cells show no statistically significant warming (see the coast card). ERA5 was compared at five points, not on the difference.
open: Why the Antofagasta station disagrees with the regional mean
cards.question: Did Antofagasta's regional-mean temperature rise faster than Los Lagos'?

cards.title: Coastal and interior MERRA-2 cells of Antofagasta show different warming trends

source.product: MERRA-2; cells classified in QGIS; CIREN DEM for cell elevations

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27); difference series

thresholds.rule: centre within 30 km of the coast

checks.source: ERA5 at 4 coastal and 5 interior cell centres
checks.scope: ERA5 and MERRA-2 at the same 9 cell centres (4 coastal, 5 interior), not regional means
checks.dependency: partially dependent: a different reanalysis that assimilates many of the same observations as MERRA-2

checks.scope: NASA regional mean recomputed on the station's months; the station is one point
checks.dependency: point observation (different spatial support); may be assimilated by the reanalyses

cards.can: No statistically significant warming was detected in the coastal MERRA-2 cells over 1980–2025 (-0.027 °C/decade, 95 % CI -0.189 to +0.135, which includes zero), while the interior cells warmed (+0.265, CI +0.143 to +0.387). The difference between the two trends is significant, and ERA5 at matching points shows the same contrast.
cards.cannot: It does not show that the coast did not warm (not significant is not 'no change'), and it does not establish a cause: coast and elevation are strongly correlated (ρ = 0.90), the elevation-range-restricted comparison is not exact matching, and coastal cells mix ocean and land.
open: Role of the cool coastal ocean (SST not yet integrated)
Falvey & Garreaud (2009) found a related contrast for 1979–2006
limitations: coastal cells mix ocean and land
exploratory, decided after seeing the regional result
cards.question: Do coastal and inland parts of Antofagasta show different warming trends?

cards.title: Magallanes precipitation: significant decline in IMERG, not reproduced by ERA5 or the Punta Arenas station

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27)

checks.scope: NASA regional mean recomputed on the station's months; the station is one point
checks.dependency: point observation (different spatial support); may be among the gauges used to adjust IMERG

checks.source: ERA5 (ECMWF reanalysis) at 5 grid points, compared with IMERG at the same points
checks.scope: ERA5 and NASA at the same five grid points (not a regional mean)
checks.dependency: partially independent: ERA5 precipitation is a model forecast field; IMERG is satellite-based and gauge-adjusted; both may use some of the same gauges indirectly

cards.can: Within IMERG, a statistically significant negative trend over 1998–2024 (significant also after adjusting for 16 regions).
cards.cannot: A significant trend in one product is not a confirmed regional drying: the station (one point) and ERA5 (five grid points) do not reproduce an equivalent conclusion.
open: IMERG is known to struggle over steep, windy terrain; whether that explains this case is not tested
cards.question: Is Magallanes getting drier, according to several products?

cards.title: Magallanes temperature: no significant trend in MERRA-2, while ERA5 and the Punta Arenas station show warming

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27)

checks.scope: NASA regional mean recomputed on the station's months; the station is one point
checks.dependency: point observation (different spatial support); may be assimilated by the reanalyses

checks.source: ERA5 (ECMWF reanalysis) at 5 grid points, compared with MERRA-2 at the same points
checks.scope: ERA5 and NASA at the same five grid points (not a regional mean)
checks.dependency: partially dependent: a different reanalysis that assimilates many of the same observations as MERRA-2

cards.can: Within MERRA-2, no statistically significant trend is detected over 1980–2025 (p = 0.969).
cards.cannot: No significant trend in MERRA-2 is not evidence of no warming: ERA5 at five grid points and the Punta Arenas station both show significant warming.
open: Why MERRA-2 differs from ERA5 here (model, observations assimilated, coastal cells) is not tested
cards.question: Is Magallanes warming, according to several products?

cards.title: Detrended rainfall and modelled root-zone soil moisture vary together in central Chile
cards.variable: IMERG precipitation vs GLDAS root-zone soil moisture

analysis.method: Pearson r of detrended yearly anomalies; effective sample size (Bretherton et al. 1999)

cards.can: Year-to-year, wetter years have wetter soils in this region.
cards.cannot: GLDAS is driven by observed precipitation, so the agreement is partly built in; it is not independent evidence or a cause.
open: River discharge (CAMELS-CL) and vegetation (MODIS) would add independent responses
cards.question: Do wet and dry years show up in the soil of central Chile?

cards.title: The number of regions with a nominally significant precipitation trend depends on the start year

analysis.method: Least squares on yearly means of monthly anomalies; lag-1 effective sample size (worst simulated false-positive rate 8.6 % at 46 years, 10.1 % at 27)
analysis.correction: none: windows are sensitivity checks, not new tests

cards.can: Precipitation trends over ~25 years depend strongly on where the record starts.
cards.cannot: The shorter window does not reveal a 'hidden' drying; choosing the window after seeing results would be selection.
open: The main (pre-registered) analysis keeps the full record
